Wellness & experiences

Movement first, then the music.

Wellness is not a side act here — it is half the brand. Morning movement opens the day, the DJs carry it, and the coffee ties it together. That combination is what makes a Coffee Party different from every other daytime event.

In the hub, wellness partners book into the same calendar as the parties, so a studio's Saturday class and a Coffee Party afternoon become one plan, not two competing ones.

New · For the owner · Add to Home Screen

Put the hub on every phone.

Anyone can add this experience to their home screen today, so it opens like an app from a Coffee Party icon. Here is exactly how — and exactly what a fully installable version requires.

iPhone (Safari)

  1. Open the published website in Safari.
  2. Tap Share.
  3. Select Add to Home Screen.
  4. Name it The Coffee Party.
  5. Tap Add.

Android (Chrome)

  1. Open the website in Chrome.
  2. Open the three-dot menu.
  3. Select Install app or Add to Home screen.
  4. Confirm.

Honest note on the full PWA

A home-screen shortcut is not a native app, and a single file cannot ship a complete installable PWA on its own — a manifest and a service worker must be separate files served from the same site. To make this page fully installable on GitHub Pages, add these two files beside index.html, plus two icon PNGs (192×192 and 512×512), and link the manifest in the page head:

1 · manifest.webmanifest

{ "name": "The Coffee Party", "short_name": "Coffee Party", "start_url": "./index.html", "display": "standalone", "background_color": "#ffffff", "theme_color": "#080808", "icons": [ { "src": "icon-192.png", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png" }, { "src": "icon-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png" } ] }

2 · service-worker.js — register it from index.html over HTTPS (GitHub Pages already serves HTTPS)

const CACHE = "coffee-party-v1"; const ASSETS = ["./", "./index.html", "./manifest.webmanifest", "./icon-192.png", "./icon-512.png"]; self.addEventListener("install", e => { e.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then(c => c.addAll(ASSETS))); }); self.addEventListener("fetch", e => { e.respondWith(caches.match(e.request) .then(r => r || fetch(e.request))); });

This page already carries the mobile metadata (theme colour, home-screen title) so the shortcut looks right the moment it is added.
